options: The line marking the boundary of the field
The area where the bowler runs up before delivery
The marked lines at each end of the pitch indicating safe ground for batsmen
The zone where fielders are not allowed to stand
easy_conceptual.correct_answer: The marked lines at each end of the pitch indicating safe ground for batsmen

easy_conceptual.text: What does an "over" consist of in cricket?
options: Six legal deliveries bowled by the same bowler
Four balls bowled from each end of the pitch
Ten runs scored by a batsman
easy_conceptual.correct_answer: Six legal deliveries bowled by the same bowler

easy_conceptual.text: What is the primary role of the wicket‑keeper?
options: To bowl fast deliveries from the opposite end
To field at the boundary and catch high balls
To stand behind the stumps and catch or stump the batsman
To act as the team captain and set field placements
easy_conceptual.correct_answer: To stand behind the stumps and catch or stump the batsman

options: A delivery that hits the batsman's helmet
An illegal delivery for which the batting side receives one extra run and the ball must be re‑bowled
A ball that lands outside the boundary line
A delivery that results in a wicket without any runs
easy_conceptual.correct_answer: An illegal delivery for which the batting side receives one extra run and the ball must be re‑bowled

options: The batsman is dismissed because the ball hits the stumps while he is outside his crease
The bowler delivers a ball that is too fast
The fielding side scores a run without the batters' consent
The batting side voluntarily ends the innings
easy_conceptual.correct_answer: The batsman is dismissed because the ball hits the stumps while he is outside his crease

options: A line that marks the edge of the pitch where the bowler must release the ball
The distance a batsman must run to score a single
The outer edge of the playing field; hitting the ball beyond it scores four or six runs
A term for the line separating the two batting ends
easy_conceptual.correct_answer: The outer edge of the playing field; hitting the ball beyond it scores four or six runs

medium_application.text: In a limited-overs match, a team uses a powerplay with only two fielders outside the 30-yard circle. Which type of bowler is most likely to be effective?

A bowler bowls a delivery that hits the batsman's helmet placed on the ground. What is the ruling?
A captain decides to bowl a spinner on a green, seaming pitch in the 20th over of a T20 match. Which factor makes this decision risky?
options: The ball will swing more on a green pitch
Spinners are more effective on dry, cracked surfaces
Green pitches favor fast bowlers due to extra seam movement
The ball will lose shine faster on a green pitch
medium_application.correct_answer: Green pitches favor fast bowlers due to extra seam movement

medium_application.text: During a Test match, a batsman scores 150 runs but faces only 120 balls. Which statistic best reflects his scoring efficiency?
A bowler has figures of 10 overs, 2 maidens, 40 runs, and 5 wickets. What is his economy rate?
In a limited‑overs game, a team needs 30 runs off the last 3 overs with 2 wickets remaining. Which batting strategy is most appropriate?
options: Target the boundaries and rotate strike
Play defensively and wait for a mistake
Try hitting sixes on every ball
medium_application.correct_answer: Target the boundaries and rotate strike

medium_application.text: A player is awarded the 'Man of the Match' after taking 4 catches, scoring 20 runs, and effecting 2 run‑outs. Which aspect of his performance most likely contributed to the award?
A bowler delivers a ball that hits the batsman's pad and goes onto the stumps. The umpire gives out bowled. Which law governs this dismissal?
A team scores 250 runs in 50 overs in a One Day International. Their run rate is 5 runs per over. If they lose 5 wickets, what is their batting average per wicket?
During a match, a bowler is reported for exceeding the permissible arm‑extension limit. Which ICC regulation does this relate to?
options: Illegal bowling action (straightening of the arm)
medium_application.correct_answer: Illegal bowling action (straightening of the arm)

medium_application.text: In a T20 match, a team sets a target of 180 runs. The opposition scores 175/9 in 20 overs. Which metric shows how close the chase was?

During a rain‑affected 30‑over match, Team B’s revised target is 180 runs. After 10 overs they are 45/2. If they want to maintain a required run rate (RRR) that is 0.5 runs per over higher than the current RRR, how many runs must they score in the next 5 overs?
